# Jolito — Product & Learner Guide

> Spoken Mexican Spanish flashcards built for active recall, spaced repetition, and real-world conversation. Jolito turns daily language practice into a fast, rewarding habit with natural audio pronunciation, instant visual typo diffs, and zero-friction keyboard reviews.

---

# Origin Story

In July 2026, my wife *(Mexican)*, our twins *(Gexican)*, and I *(German)* moved to Mexico City. I started learning Spanish at the [International House in Condesa](https://ihmexico.mx/). The classes were fantastic—but memorizing vocabulary? **My archenemy.** The absolute worst part of learning a new language!

I needed what I learned in class and heard on the streets to stick. While Anki provided the unbeatable spaced repetition algorithm needed for long-term retention, manually creating rich cards—clipping audio, finding pictures, and wrestling templates—felt like an exhausting chore at the end of a long day. Gamified apps looked great and sounded natural, but locked learners into rigid beginner courses with zero control over the real-world phrases they actually wanted to speak.

I built Jolito to make memorization something to look forward to: **fast, tactile, immersive**. Spaced repetition games your memory—**legally!** It resurfaces words just before you forget them, so they stick almost effortlessly.

Memorization and I have become friends!

---

# Product Overview

Jolito blends the proven power of spaced repetition flashcards with the audio immersion and friction-free flow of a modern practice app. Built for mastering real-world Mexican Spanish, Jolito turns daily language practice into a fast, rewarding habit—online or offline.

## Why Another Flashcard App?

- **Anki** is unbeatable for spaced repetition, but creating rich language cards with natural audio, reciprocal directions, and context requires tedious template configuration and manual media clipping.
- **Duolingo** makes daily practice inviting, but locks learners into rigid multiple-choice curricula without control over the real-world phrases they actually want to learn.
- **Jolito** delivers the speed and control of spaced repetition with zero-friction authoring, native Mexican Spanish audio, focused grammar drills, curated starter packs, and keyboard-first or gesture-driven typed active recall.

---

# Core Principles & Learning Design

1. **AI proposes; the learner authors:** Jolito removes repetitive work by suggesting translations, pronunciations, audio, and context, while the learner stays in control.
2. **Production, not recognition:** Learners type answers before revealing the canonical response. Self-evaluation remains authoritative because natural language has valid alternatives.
3. **Make it flow:** New cards focus inputs automatically; prompt audio plays automatically; keyboard shortcuts (`Enter` to reveal, `1`–`4` to grade, `Space` for audio) and mobile swipe gestures carry the learner through review with zero friction.
4. **Focused grammar practice:** Dedicated, bite-sized training for tricky Mexican Spanish conjugations—Pretérito Indefinido, Pretérito Perfecto Compuesto, and Gerundio—with numbered accent shortcuts and subject-verb matching.
5. **Curated starter packs:** Built-in decks (Top Connectors, Adjectives, Idioms, Adverbs) that merge semantically into your deck without overwriting progress.
6. **Words and chunks are equally valid:** A card may be a single word, an idiom, or any useful language chunk.
7. **Two-way by default, independently editable:** Most cards create linked Spanish ↔ English and English ↔ Spanish practice cards with side-by-side previews.
8. **Offline is a first-class requirement:** Review, card creation, audio, and grammar practice work completely without an internet connection using local browser storage and service worker caching. Changes sync unobtrusively with Supabase when connected.
9. **Context is available, never in the way:** Concise answers serve as the primary card target, while an optional context drawer provides richer explanations, grammar notes, and CDMX slang variants.
10. **Use modes in concert:** Text, visuals, and audio clarify and reinforce one another without competing for attention.

---

# Keyboard Controls & Review Flow

- `Enter`: Reveal canonical answer / submit response
- `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`: Self-grade recall (**1: Again**, **2: Hard**, **3: Good**, **4: Easy**)
- `Space`: Replay pronunciation audio (prompt before reveal, expected answer after reveal)
- Mobile Gestures: Swipe up to reveal, swipe horizontally to grade with continuous spring settling.
- Autofocus: Inputs automatically focus on each new card so hands never need to leave the keyboard.
